query: Explain the difference between `git merge` and `git rebase` in two short paragraphs, with one sentence on when to prefer each.
result:
`git merge` joins two branches by creating a new merge commit that has both branches as parents. Existing commits are never changed, so the full history of what happened and when is preserved. The cost is that a busy project can end up with a branching graph full of merge commits. Prefer merge when the branch is shared with others or when you want the record of how work was integrated.

`git rebase` instead takes your commits and replays them on top of another branch's latest commit, so the result reads as one straight line. Replaying creates new commits with new hashes, which rewrites history. That is safe on a local branch you haven't pushed, but rebasing a branch others have pulled forces them to reconcile and usually requires a force push. Prefer rebase to tidy your own unpushed feature branch before you share it.
